propositions: The enrich drain holds its advisory lock across no-timeout LLM calls (437s, 131s observed), creating single-flight bottleneck where every spawned drain child exits skipped; standing backlog ~1,046 entries.

Restructure drain() into three phases: COLLECT (under lock; concurrency guard capped 3 drainers, batch clamp lease_ttl_s // 40 ≈ 20-25 items), ENRICH (lock-free LLM calls), FINALIZE (revalidate content-hash; stale entries re-enqueued with soak 0, else emit + done).

Raise DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH from 5 to 20 with lease-derived clamp, enabling up to 3 concurrent drainers × ~20 items/batch with lock held only 1.5-2.9s (collect phase), yielding ~9x per-item lock-cost reduction and throughput exceeding enqueue rate.
Stale-at-writeback entries (edited between claim and finalize) skip digest emit, re-enqueue with soak 0 immediate retry, and are tracked as stale_skipped in drain summary.

Concurrent drainers bounded by guard: 4th drainer skips with concurrency-cap when 3 distinct live-lease drainer claims exist; existing per-write spawned drain children become productive without new spawner/scheduler.

Existing pre-change contracts (store write lock, queue schema ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE, has_pending_enrichment, MCP surface, failure disposition) unchanged; hung LLM provider blocks only its batch instead of wedging all drainers.
